title.narrative: Marketing Innovations for Sustainable Health Development

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Marketing Innovations for Sustainable Health Development activity continues to meet market demand for family planning, health, and nutrition products and services through its service and distribution networks. USAID helped establish the Social Marketing Company (SMC) in 1974 - now a sustainable local organization with over $150 million in annual revenue. Since 2016, USAID's partnership with SMC has been through a Global Development Alliance that currently leverages $17 USD for every $1 USD spent by USAID. Using FY 2024 funds, SMC will utilize its vast network of sales agents and service delivery outlets to deliver public health products. The network includes private physicians, pharmacists, non-graduate medical practitioners, and rural female community sales agents. This network will deliver services such as growth monitoring and promotion for children under five; nutrition counseling; counseling to delay early marriage and pregnancy; and referring gender-based violence survivors to care centers. Network providers will sell SMC-branded commodities such as contraceptives; oral rehydration salts; maternal and child micronutrient products; safe delivery kits; menstrual hygiene products; electrolyte drinks; and micronutrient fortified biscuits. SMC will create new private sector partnerships to expand its products and services, eventually ending its reliance on USAID funds. The activity supports goal three of the Joint Strategic Plan and ICS Mission Objective three. The activity will advance the Indo-Pacific Strategy by working with GoB to intensify efforts to prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases.FY 2024 funding will contribute to Adaptation Indirect ($250k), Innovation (200k), Gender Equality ($1.2m), GBV ($100k),GBV-CEFM ($200k), GFS ($400k), Cross-Cutting HSS ($250k), MHPSS($150k), MSN ($400k), Macronutrients ($300k of which Vit A is $200k), PGI-Indirect Health ($1.5m), PSE ($400k) and WASH ($50k) issues.
